THE PHYSICS

A = Z + N · charge = Z − electrons

Changing protons changes the element. Changing neutrons changes the isotope. Changing electrons changes the charge while leaving the element and mass number unchanged.

TRY AN EXPERIMENT

Make a carbon ion

Keep 6 protons and 6 neutrons. Remove two electrons, then add one neutron. Which labels change each time?

Inside this model +

A counting model for the first ten elements, not a nuclear or quantum dynamics simulation. Electron shell counts use a simplified 2, 8, then outer-shell arrangement. Dots show counts rather than electron trajectories. Particle choices can include unstable nuclei or unbound ions; this model does not predict stability, binding, decay, or electron configurations for every charged state.

Atomic number Z = proton count. Mass number A = protons + neutrons. Net charge in units of e = protons − electrons.
